High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:145150
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 28445 of 2023

Applicant :- Sarbar Shambhu @ Labh Singh
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Pradeep Kumar Shukla
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Sri Pradeep Kumar learned AGA apprised the Court that on 23.6.2023 notice has been served to the informant.
Despite service of notice none appeared on behalf of the informant.
2. Heard Sri R. K. Vaish, Advocate holding brief of Sri Pradeep Kumar Shukla, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Pradeep Kumar, learned AGA for the State-respondent.

3. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 7 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)N, 506 IPC and 5L/6 POCSO Act, Police Station Aliganj,
District Bareily, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

4. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and his family members and according to the FIR on 18.1.2023, applicant alongwith his family members after entering in the house of the informant abducted his minor daughter aged about 16 years.

sentences.text:
5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the entire allegation of abduction made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and this fact is evident from the statement of the victim recorded under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. in which victim categorically stated that she according to her own wish had gone alongwith the applicant and therefore, statement of the victim recorded under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. totally belies the version of FIR.
6.
He further submitted that even as per school record, victim was around seventeen years nine months old at the time of incident.
He further submitted thatapplicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 23.1.2023 i.e. for more than six months, therefore, he may be released on bail.

7. Per contra, learned AGA although opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that even as per the school record, victim was at the verge of majority and she in her both the statements recorded under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. did not state against the applicant.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. Considering the fact that even as per school record, victim was 17 years and 9 months and she in her both the statements recorded under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. stated that she had gone alongwith the applicant and also performed marriage with him, in my view, applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
10. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant-Sarbar Shambhu @ Labh Singh, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
12. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

13. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
